entry.description: Cycle Double Cover Conjecture. Every finite loopless bridgeless undirected multigraph has a multiset of cycles covering every edge exactly twice. The AI-generated proof now has a public Lean formalization and independent expert expositions by Jim Geelen and Sang-il Oum.
entry.anchor_claim: Cycle Double Cover Conjecture: every finite bridgeless graph has a multiset of cycles covering every edge exactly twice.

entry.advance_rationale: The announced proof claims to establish the full conjecture for every finite bridgeless graph.

entry.resistance_rationale: The independent 1973 and 1979 formulations were followed by many distinct partial-result programs and surveys, amply satisfying the two-prior-attempt criterion.

entry.description: Jacobian Conjecture. An explicit polynomial map from C^3 to C^3 has constant nonzero Jacobian determinant but is not injective, disproving the unrestricted conjecture in dimension three and hence every higher dimension. Independent exact symbolic checks and subsequent mathematical analyses verify the announced map.
entry.anchor_claim: An explicit three-dimensional polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant and multiple preimages disproves the unrestricted Jacobian Conjecture in every dimension at least three.
entry.prior_rationale: Keller framed the Jacobian Conjecture in 1939, and the announced map directly targets its dimension-three case.
entry.advance_rationale: If validated, one explicit noninjective constant-Jacobian map completely disproves the universal conjecture in dimensions three and above.
entry.scope_rationale: The claim is witnessed by one explicit polynomial map, so it does not receive the separate general-scope point even though standard extension propagates the consequence to higher dimensions.
entry.resistance_rationale: The Jacobian Conjecture has multiple independent reduction, special-case, and attempted-solution literatures spanning decades, well beyond the two-attempt threshold.
entry.age_rationale: Elapsed duration is computed from the coded framing and solution dates; it is not a capability claim.

entry.description: crouzeix's conjecture for complex matrices. shanmu jin's first-public repository and superseding v4 preprint report the sharp constant-2 spectral-set theorem in every finite dimension. the preprint specifically attributes the central scaled-conjugate-eigenvalue and origin sampling idea in the matrix herglotz-kernel argument to openai chatgpt. jin's repository reports a lean formalization and computational and adversarial audits; lorist and schwenninger independently published an alternative bounded-operator proof that corroborates and generalizes the same finite-dimensional claim. this automation did not execute or replay formal artifacts.
entry.anchor_claim: For every n-by-n complex matrix A, every polynomial p satisfies ||p(A)|| at most 2 max over z in W(A) of |p(z)|; the same estimate holds for functions holomorphic near W(A), so W(A) is a 2-spectral set and the universal constant 2 is sharp.
entry.prior_rationale: Crouzeix formulated the exact universal constant-2 numerical-range spectral-set conjecture in 2004.
entry.advance_rationale: The source reports a complete affirmative resolution with the conjectured sharp universal constant.
entry.scope_rationale: The theorem applies uniformly to complex matrices of every finite dimension and the stated holomorphic functional calculus.
entry.resistance_rationale: Multiple published special-class results and successive universal bounds document independent sustained attacks on the exact conjecture.
entry.age_rationale: Elapsed duration is computed from the coded framing and solution dates; it is not a capability claim.
